failure.backupsUnavailable: {path} could not be opened, so ScriptDock is not keeping a history of your settings and hidden scripts in this session. The file was left unchanged. Repair or move it, then start ScriptDock again.
failure.keptSettings: Some settings in {path} could not be used: {keys}. ScriptDock is using the built-in values for these and keeps the stored values unchanged in the file. Correct them in the file, or choose new values in Settings to replace them.
failure.launchStopped: ScriptDock left these files unchanged and has not opened scripts or changed settings. For a file a newer version saved, use that version. Otherwise repair the file, restore it from a backup, or move it away to start fresh, then start ScriptDock again.
failure.recordsUnavailable: {path} could not be opened, so ScriptDock is not recording run history in this session, and Recent and Records may be empty. The file was left unchanged. Repair or move it, then start ScriptDock again.
failure.refusedNewer: {path} was saved by a newer version of ScriptDock, and this version cannot read it.
failure.rootPicker: The folder picker could not be opened. Your root directories are unchanged; try adding a directory again.
failure.scriptStart: The script could not be started. Check the session log for details, then try again.
failure.scriptStartPermission: The script could not be started. Check that ScriptDock can run it, then try again.
failure.startupStorage: ScriptDock cannot use its storage location, so it has not opened scripts or changed settings. Repair the SCRIPTDOCK_DATA_DIR location or its permissions, then start ScriptDock again.

ignoreNote.git: Git’s own data for a repository.
ignoreNote.nodeModules: Packages that npm and other JavaScript tools install.
ignoreNote.dotnetBin: .NET build output in bin/Debug and bin/Release. A plain bin folder is still scanned.
ignoreNote.target: Build output from Cargo (Rust) and Maven (Java).
ignoreNote.vendor: Packages installed by Composer (PHP), Go and Bundler (Ruby).
ignoreNote.trash: Your Trash on a Mac. Holds what you deleted.
ignoreNote.trashes: A drive’s Trash on a Mac. Holds what was deleted from that drive.
ignoreNote.macosx: Mac-only data left over from unzipping a ZIP made on a Mac.
ignoreNote.fseventsd: macOS’s record of changes on a drive.
ignoreNote.temporaryItems: Temporary files macOS keeps on a drive.
ignoreNote.documentRevisions: Older versions of documents, kept by macOS on a drive.
ignoreNote.mobileBackups: Time Machine snapshots kept on the Mac itself (older macOS).
ignoreNote.appleDouble: Mac-only data kept by a file server or a drive that isn’t Mac-formatted.
ignoreNote.recycleBin: A drive’s Recycle Bin. Holds what was deleted from that drive.
ignoreNote.oldRecycleBin: A drive’s Recycle Bin from older Windows.
ignoreNote.systemVolume: Windows’ restore points and search index for a drive.

settings.extensionSpaces: An extension can’t contain spaces or line breaks.
settings.extensionsHint: Separate extensions with commas, such as .command, .sh.
settings.extensionsRequired: Add at least one extension; with none, a scan finds nothing.
settings.ignorePatternsHint: Scanning skips what these patterns match, ignoring case; a trailing / means folders only. A wildcard pattern matches a name in any folder, unless a / before its end anchors it at the root directory. A regular expression is searched for anywhere in the full path.
settings.ignorePatternsEmpty: No ignore patterns, so every folder is scanned.
settings.patternInvalidRegex: This is not a valid regular expression.
settings.nonZeroExitIsError: Treat an exit code other than 0 as an error
settings.nonZeroExitIsErrorHint: When this is on, a run that ends with a code other than 0 shows its code in red in Recent, and Records lists it as an error. Either way, Records keeps the code in the run’s details.
settings.patternInvalid: This is not a valid pattern.
settings.patternMultiline: A pattern must be a single line.
